newsitem.title: UK: Marks takes another look at Japanese market.
newsitem.headline: Marks takes another look at Japanese market.

text.p: British retailer Marks & Spencer Plc said on Tuesday it is looking again at the Japanese market, but has no immediate plans to open stores there.

Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury, responding to questions at a news conference on the company's results, said M&S had decided against moving into Japan three years ago, because the cost of entry in terms of sites and labour was prohibitive.
"The situation has eased a little and we're having another look at that market," he said.
But he said with other opportunities for expansion overseas it would not be sensible to enter Japan if it was going to prove a tough market to crack.
M&S has stores in North America, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain, France and Germany, plus franchise operations in 22 countries.
Its first store in Germany in Cologne opened last autumn and Greenbury said it had been trading well, slightly above estimates.
